newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian move to Abuja slows business.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian move to Abuja slows business.

text.p: Nigeria's umbrella trade group said on Tuesday the movement of several state agencies to the inland capital Abuja from Lagos was adversely affecting business, the national news agency reported.

Among the agencies that have moved their headquarters to Abuja in compliance with a government order are Nigerian Ports Authority, Nigerian Maritime Authority and the Nigerian Shippers Council whose activities are in the coastal southern areas and relate to the business community on a daily basis.

Business executives were having to shuttle between Lagos and Abuja at great cost to the economy, the Nigerian Association of Chambers and Commerce, Industry, Mines and Agriculture (NACCIMA) said in a 1997 pre-budget memorandum sent to the government.

NACCIMA said it was not against moving the agencies to Abuja, but suggested their operations be decentralised to enable officials in Lagos, Port Harcourt and Warri, all in the south, take major on-the-spot decisions that affect businesses.
Military ruler General Sani Abacha gave an October deadline to all federal ministries and government agencies to move their headquarters to Abuja and operate from there.
